name: The Lungfish Circuit (Flooded Ruins Urbex League)
description: Where the Carcass Tours follow Old Chicago's dry ruins, the Lungfish Circuit specializes in M88's flooded underzones — the submerged lower levels of pre-Meridian Chicago's infrastructure that sank during the 2140s Lake Michigan overflow events, now a silent ecosystem of drowned office towers, buried transit lines, and collapsed residential blocks accessible only by diving or via pressurized entry points. Circuit members, called Lungfish, document their dives through waterproofed BCI capture rigs and share footage on closed Underworld forums under the handle-system called Gill Tags. The most celebrated dive in Circuit history was Piotr Makinde-Svensson's 2218 descent into the confirmed location of the old Chicago Cultural Center, still largely intact beneath forty meters of silted water.
cultural_impact: Lungfish footage has quietly become some of the most-watched content on M88's Underworld, sparking a broader cultural fascination with the drowned pre-corp city as a kind of collective inheritance that no corponation can claim or monetize.
key_figures: The Archivist (anonymous editor of the Gill Tag compendium)
locations: Pressurized Entry Point 7, Shelf Sector 12 (primary access node)
The Surface — Lungfish gathering bar, Tier 2 Lakeward district
story_hooks: A Lungfish diver surfaces from a routine dive claiming to have seen lights moving in the flooded ruins — deliberate, patterned lights — and refuses to go back down alone.
Someone is paying extremely well for footage of a specific flooded building, a former corporate archive, and the Lungfish who took the job haven't resurfaced in two weeks.
The Circuit discovers a pressurized habitat someone has been living in beneath the water for an unknown period of time — and whoever it is has been there long enough to decorate.
